title: The Night Everyone Forgot the Moon

shots.visual_event: Meera, Maya, and quadruped Tick align thirteen station mirrors into a ring around the brass handbell.
shots.dialogue_audio: Maya: “One signal cost a minute. Two may cost the city.”

shots.visual_event: Meera rings anyway. Above them the full moon flickers like a faulty lamp while Arin appears across all mirrors.
shots.dialogue_audio: Meera: “Arin, the route says Car Four.”

shots.visual_event: Arin shouts back from the train as Nila’s glowing cracks spread across the mirrored sky.
shots.dialogue_audio: Arin: “Don’t call again. It charges everyone.”

shots.visual_event: The signal breaks. People across the city look up at a bright circle they can see but cannot name.
shots.dialogue_audio: Child in street: “What is that light?”

shots.visual_event: Maya opens a schoolbook: every moon illustration remains, but every printed label is blank under clean editorial masking.
Meera writes MOON on her palm before she forgets, then looks up and says the word to Tick.
